summary: @hubsync/web-sdk-react preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (_0xXXXX identifier scheme) and, when bun is not already on PATH, downloads the Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts and chmods the bun binary, then invokes it against the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727,680-byte Bun-compiled bundle (starts with `// @bun @bun-cjs`) using obfuscator.io-style string-array rotation; it is not referenced from dist/index.js and is only executed via the dropped Bun interpreter. This alternate-runtime dropper pattern executes an opaque bundled payload on the installer's machine at `npm install` time, bypassing Node-based static analysis. The package name `@hubsync/web-sdk-react` and its README (`npm i -S @verdocs/web-sdk-react`) impersonate the unrelated legitimate Verdocs Web SDK; the genuine Verdocs SDK has no preinstall hook, no Bun download, and no math_init.js. The malicious lifecycle script and payload were grafted onto a copy of the Verdocs SDK under an unrelated scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
